uncited: The Point-in-Box Inclusion Test determines which points from a given array lie within an orthogonal bounding box.
It serves as the core primitive for [Voxel Occupancy Test](1281-voxel-occupancy-test.md), filtering points to identify voxel occupancy.
Unlike [3D Filled Circle Kernel Generation](1520-3d-filled-circle-kernel-generation.md) which uses distance metrics, this method relies on strict axis-aligned boundary checks.
It differs from [Sparse AABB Collision Test](3047-sparse-aabb-collision-test.md) by operating on a static point array rather than dynamic collision shapes.
- `box`: An orthogonal bounding box defined by minimum bounds `min` and maximum bounds `max` for each dimension $d \in \{x, y, z\}$.
- The input array `PP` is partitioned such that the first `n_in` points are inside, and the remaining are outside.
Increment `l` while `l < n` and point `PP[l]` is inside the box on all dimensions.
Decrement `r` while `r >= 0` and point `PP[r]` is NOT inside the box on all dimensions.
- Points exactly on the boundary are considered inside (inclusive check).
Finds the spatial dimension with the largest spread among all dimensions in a point set before partitioning.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(n)$ in the worst case, as each point is visited at most once by the two pointers.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary space if performed in-place.
Performance degrades if the box is very small or very large relative to the point distribution, though the linear scan remains constant time.
Originated in the context of 3D reconstruction and dual contouring implementations, specifically within the `DualContouring-3DRendring` project.
